subject: astronaut spacewalk
title: Space Has a Smell, and Astronauts Say It's Seared Steak and Hot Metal

scenes.text: Space has a smell. Astronauts say it's seared steak.
Not out there. In a vacuum you can't smell anything, and inside the suit it smells of plastic.
The smell hits when they come back in and take the helmet off. It clings to the suit, the gloves, the tools.
Hot metal. Welding fumes. Burnt steak. Spent gunpowder. One astronaut said he'll never forget it.
The best guess: sunlight splits oxygen into single atoms, which stick to the suit and react when air hits them.
scenes.keywords: sun flare over earth from space

scenes.text: NASA hired a chemist to recreate it so trainees wouldn't be surprised. He bottled it. You can buy space as a perfume.

description:
Astronauts cannot smell anything in the vacuum of space, but after a spacewalk their suits, gloves and tools carry a strong odour they describe as seared steak, hot metal, welding fumes and spent gunpowder.
The leading explanation is atomic oxygen: ultraviolet sunlight splits oxygen molecules into single atoms that cling to the suit and react once back in the airlock. NASA hired chemist Steve Pearce in 2008 to recreate the smell for training, and he later helped launch it as the perfume Eau de Space.
What do you think space should smell like? Comment below.
first_comment: Astronaut Don Pettit said the space station itself smells like half machine shop, half engine room, half laboratory. Which space question should we answer next?
